title: EFC — Introduction to Entropy in Cosmic Evolution
description: Introductory overview of entropy’s role in cosmic evolution within the Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) framework. It outlines how entropy underpins the arrow of time, informs the formation of large-scale structure and black hole thermodynamics, and guides the universe toward thermodynamic equilibrium, linking these themes to energy flow and time–space dynamics.

key_results.main_finding: Entropy is presented as the directional driver of cosmic evolution, shaping structure formation, black-hole thermodynamics, and the universe’s progression toward thermodynamic equilibrium within the EFC framework.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-precision CMB and early-universe probes demonstrate the initial cosmic state was near maximum entropy rather than low entropy, contradicting the paper’s premise.

KC2: Observations across black-hole mass scales falsify the area–entropy relation (e.g., entropy does not scale with event-horizon area), undermining the claim that black holes are maximal-entropy objects.
KC3: A comprehensive cosmic entropy inventory shows a sustained net decrease in total entropy from high to low redshift, violating the asserted global increase and arrow of time in cosmic evolution.

KC4: Joint simulation–observation studies establish that matter clustering proceeds without associated increases in coarse-grained entropy or energy dispersal, contradicting the claim that entropy drives large-scale structure formation.
KC5: Empirical evidence of a long-term cosmic engine enabling indefinite extraction of usable work without entropy production, invalidating the heat-death end state.
